Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page:** South Carolina State Climatology Office – “Tropical Storms and Hurricanes: 1950-1959”  
URL: https://www.dnr.sc.gov/climate/sco/Tropics/1950s.php  

**Evidence**  

| Year | Dates in S.C. | Landfall Area | Category | Storm Track Map | Comments | Rainfall Mention |
|------|---------------|---------------|----------|-----------------|----------|------------------|
| 1950 | Oct 18‑19 | Miami, FL | H‑3 | King | “The storm weakened over S.C. upper Piedmont; heavy rains and gale force winds” | – |
| 1950 | Oct 25 | Cedar Key, FL | H | Love | “The storm delivered moderate to heavy intermittent rain.” | – |
| 1952 | Aug 30‑31 | Beaufort, S.C. | H‑1 | Able | “The storm entered the coast of S.C. near Beaufort with 80‑90 mph winds and excessive rains. Two storm‑related deaths.” | – |
| 1953 | Aug 31‑Sept 1 | Savannah, GA | T.S. | TS#3 | “North‑northeast across S.C. as a weak TS.” | – |
| 1953 | Sept 20‑21 | Cedar Key, FL | T.S. | TS#7 | “Tracked across north Fla., East Ga., and offshore S.C. coast. Scattered rainfall, moderate winds.” | – |
| 1953 | Sept 27 | Panama City, FL | H‑1 | Florence | “Northeast over Fla., Ga.; weakened to extratropical storm. Gale winds; heavy to excessive rainfall.” | high rainfall (exact inches not stated) |
| 1954 | Oct 15 | SC‑NC State line | H‑4 | Hazel | “One of the most stongest hurricanes to hit South Carolina… Storm surge: 16.9 ft… Moved northward off the coast of SC… center passing between 90 and miles east of Charleston….” | – |
| 1955 | Aug 11‑12 | Cape Lookout, NC | H‑3 | Connie | “No hurricane force winds were reported. Rain squalls occurred over lower part of the State. Tides were 1‑2 ft higher than normal along the coast.” | – |
| 1955 | Aug 17 | Wilmington, NC | H‑1 | Diane | “Moved North‑northwest into N.C.; heavy rains, high tides, $100,000 damage in S.C.” | – |
| 1955 | Sept 18‑19 | Morehead City, NC | H‑3 | Ione | “Moved northward off the SC coast and was about 150 miles east of Myrtle Beach.” | – |
| 1956 | Sept 21‑24 | Fort Walton Beach, FL | H‑1 | Flossy | “Flossy became extratropical on the 25th over Georgia… and continued northeastward across eastern South Carolina, dropping heavy rain throughout its path and breaking a drought in the northeast.” | – |
| 1958 | Sept 27 | – | H | Helene | “Approached north‑coastal area, curved northeast. Minor damage reported.” | – |
| 1959 | May 31‑Jun 3 | Week’s Island, LA | T.S. | Arlene | “Rain event.” | – |
| 1959 | Jul 8‑9 | McClellanville, S.C. | H‑1 | Cindy | “Heavy rains ( 10 inches in some areas) caused considerable flooding. Highest reported winds were 60‑65 mph.” | 10 in |
| 1959 | Sept 29 | St. Helena Is., S.C. | H‑4 | Gracie | “Heavy crop damage; moderate to heavy flooding from 6‑8 inches of rainfall.” | 6‑8 in |

**Coverage**  
The page lists every tropical storm or hurricane that interacted with South Carolina during the 1950s and includes dates, landfall areas, categories, and concise commentaries on track, winds, rainfall, and damage. The table is complete for the decade 1950‑1959 as presented. The page only provides high‑level notes; it does not give detailed track figures or rainfall totals beyond the few qualitative statements cited.

**Missing**  

* List of storms whose track passed within **15 nautical miles** of Myrtle Beach, SC (no explicit evidence of such proximity here).  
* Maximum rainfall totals of **≥ 15 inches** for any storm in the contiguous United States (only 10 in for Cindy and 6‑8 in for Gracie are mentioned).
